NEW WORST-CASE INSTANCE, found by execution rather than by reading, and arguably worse than the swapped-argument case I ranked first.

  rdm(crossnobis_plan)
  Error: RDM requires a geometry plan or complete effect form.

The user holds an object of class effect_crossnobis_plan, created by calling a function named plan_crossnobis, and is told the verb requires a plan. The message names a category the object appears to satisfy and rejects it anyway. Nothing indicates a different kind of plan is meant; nothing names crossnobis() as the verb that does accept the object.

This is the same defect class as the R/scope.R:249-251 case - the message describes the requirement rather than the mismatch - but the failure mode is worse, because here the message and the object's own class name appear to AGREE. A user reading it concludes they built the plan incorrectly. In the swapped-argument case at least the message is merely unhelpful; here it actively supports a false diagnosis.

Both share one fix, which is the general form of the recommendation on this bead: name what was received, not only what was required. Detail on bd-01KZYAV952F3MJFDWR43FH8XTV.
